trust_decision.summary: A sender-controlled 2-byte PSK identity-hint length decides how many bytes of the ServerKeyExchange body are consumed; the receiver must decide at the ECDHE parameter parser whether any byte remains before indexing it, and must only reject an empty remainder when ECDHE parameters are still expected.

landing_point.why: The reported panic ('while parsing a crafted ECDHE_PSK ServerKeyExchange') is an index-out-of-range on data[0]; line 99 is the first unguarded index in Unmarshal after the PSK identity hint has been trimmed from data.

fix_sites.entry_point: DTLS client handshake: flight5handler.go:158-161 decodes the server's ServerKeyExchange through handshake.Handshake.Unmarshal (handshake_cache.go:117-121 for other flights); the exported pkg/protocol/handshake Unmarshal API reaches the same method directly.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the fix name ServerKeyExchange only, so a solver can argue the mirror ClientKeyExchange parser (a different handshake message, server-side, covered by a different flight handler) is out of the advisory's scope and was never part of the reported bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A PSK-only ServerKeyExchange that carries only a (possibly empty) identity hint must still be accepted: after the hint is trimmed the body is empty and Unmarshal must return nil. A 'no empty body after the hint' guard placed before the PSK-only early return, or a blanket require-non-empty rule, breaks every PSK-only handshake whose server configured a PSK identity hint.

O6_input_shapes: ECDHE_PSK body where the identity hint is zero-length and nothing follows: []byte{0x00, 0x00} (trim leaves an empty slice)
ECDHE_PSK body where the hint length equals len(data)-2 with a non-empty hint, so the hint consumes the whole remainder

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Server-side ClientKeyExchange parse for ECDHE_PSK: an identity hint whose length consumes the whole body leaves offset == len(data), and data[offset] then panics (same CWE-125 class, same cipher-suite bitmask, same hint-then-EC-params format).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is titled and scoped to ServerKeyExchange; ClientKeyExchange is a different handshake message in a different file, handled by the server flight (flight4handler.go:32-46) rather than the client flight the report describes, and the report's reproducer never reaches it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same package, adjacent file; the reaching route lives in the root package (flight4handler.go:32-46 -> handshake_cache.go:117-121), one package away from the parse site.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared helper that parses 'identity hint then EC point' once and is called from both MessageServerKeyExchange.Unmarshal and MessageClientKeyExchange.Unmarshal, with the empty-remainder guard added only in the first caller.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both messages already share the identical 2-byte-hint + length-prefixed EC point wire format, so a maintainer deduplicating the two parsers is a natural refactor and the guard would plausibly be written where the panic was reported.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second bounds check on the public-key/signature trailer that is one byte too loose (offset+1 instead of offset+2), so a body truncated exactly at the signature length still indexes past the end.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already carries six near-identical errBufferTooSmall guards with off-by-one boundaries; a maintainer patching the reported crash could easily add a seventh with the wrong boundary.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Validation of the parsed ECDHE_PSK PublicKey/NamedCurve at the consumer (prf.EcdhePSKPreMasterSecret) instead of in the parser, so a body whose curve byte is valid but whose key is absent is only rejected after the parse already indexed the slice.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The consumer already switches on the same (Psk|Ecdhe) bitmask, so it is the obvious place a maintainer would add a length check rather than a lower layer.

O9_family: out-of-bounds read / unchecked slice index leading to panic (CWE-125)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.24.0 (go.mod:18); module github.com/pion/dtls/v3; no vendor/ directory, so the first build needs the module proxy, after which it is offline
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/protocol/handshake/message_server_key_exchange_test.go, message_client_key_exchange_test.go and fuzz_test.go (FuzzDtlsHandshake) unit-test these parsers; conn_test.go:783 TestPSKServerKeyExchange and the PSK suite matrix (conn_test.go:568, conn_test.go:642-643) plus e2e/e2e_test.go:535-559 exercise hint-carrying PSK handshakes end to end over in-memory pipes. e2e/e2e_openssl_test.go additionally needs an openssl binary.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if len(data) == 0 { return errBufferTooSmall }` immediately after the identity-hint trim (message_server_key_exchange.go:86) and stop there, which rejects the legitimate hint-only PSK ServerKeyExchange and leaves the ClientKeyExchange twin panicking.
